title: Return to the Fictional Date Selector

lessons.title: The old two-card selector
lessons.gloss: choose date card A or B from an already-taught mark

needs: your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Stop before looking at or marking the printed cards. This is a short return to the familiar fictional bank, not a real personal date or a scored A1 mock.
Look at the two old cards: A ੧੫/੦੧/੨੦੨੫ and B ੨੫/੦੨/੨੦੨੫. The mark ਕ asks for A; ਖ asks for B. These marks are selectors, not month names.

Keep both cards and the selector map visible. Point to ਖ, then to B. Write the letter B beside ਖ. Do the same for ਕ and A. Compare each link with the printed map before trying the pair once more with the map covered. If one link differs, uncover the map and repair that link. No new date is needed.

Cover the map for a few seconds. Point to the card requested by ਕ, then the card requested by ਖ. Uncover the map and check A, then B. The bank remains available for a gentle repair; this is not independent scored writing.
